propositions: The completion verifier returns non-deterministic PASS/FAIL verdicts on identical inputs (same ticket, code, criteria) within minutes, flipping between pass and fail-with-unmet-criteria across runs without intervening changes.

The verifier's test-existence judgments are the concentrated locus of non-determinism: it marks 'verified by a test' criteria unmet by falsely claiming tests do not exist when they do exist in the tree (e.g. ad9f test files and 4de6::test_default_close_pins_head_across_a_concurrent_commit).

The root cause is variable free-form search strategy: the LLM agent issues unpredictable semantic/regex queries against a literal-substring search tool, causing runs to either find tests (by ticket-id search) or conclude absence (by failed semantic queries), independent of whether tests exist.
The COMPLETION_VERDICT sidecar lacks verified_at_sha and trace_id fields, making stored records undiagnosable — two runs cannot be proven to have identical input from the record alone.

Non-deterministic false-NEGATIVEs (spurious FAIL) block legitimate completions and waste billable LLM runs; non-deterministic false-POSITIVEs (spurious PASS) undermine the attestation integrity of the close gate.
The flaky FAIL behavior interacts badly with the completion close mechanics, adding retry overhead and confusion when gate verdicts flip on no intervening change.
